text:
maria: noticed a weird skew in canary A/B results — the canary is getting ~2x traffic for some customers even though weight=0.05. digging in now :thinking_face:
jon: ugh, that sounds like header normalization or cookie sticky overlap. any pattern on which customers?
maria: mostly mobile apps behind CDN, traffic tends to have X-Client-Id header and a session cookie. the splitter uses header-first then weighted fallback. suspect hash mixing when header present and cookie absent.
kevin: can you paste the route match config? maybe the header-to-cohort mapping is creating a supersample.
maria: here is the relevant route block we use in prod (sanitized):
```json
{
  "matcher": [
    {"type": "header", "name": "X-Client-Id", "extract": "client_id"},
    {"type": "cookie", "name": "session_id", "extract": "sid"}
  ],
  "split": [
    {"id": "canary-v2", "weight": 0.05, "by": "hash(client_id || sid)"},
    {"id": "stable", "weight": 0.95}
  ]
}
```
jon: ah — `hash(client_id || sid)` will bias when client_id exists and sid empty. concatenation order and empty string handling can skew. we should use a deterministic join with a separator and fallback to a random seed when both are missing.
tanya: we also saw entropy collapse when CDN strips headers then re-injects different values. need to guard by normalizing header case and trimming whitespace. small differences change the hash.
kevin: proposal: change routing logic to compute a canonical "cohort_key": prefer client_id, else session_id, else fallback random seed scoped to request_id. then compute murmur3(cohort_key) % 10000 to pick bucket. also add a residual bucket for mis-routed requests so weight sums remain stable.
maria: sketch config: ```json
{"cohort_priority":["client_id","sid"], "residual_bucket":"stable_residual", "sampling_mod":10000}
```
jon: sounds good. telemetry note: instrument `routing.choice` with tags {cohort_source, bucket, was_residual:true/false} and a histogram for `cohort_entropy` so we can see collapsed distributions.
tanya: dashboard: add a per-route small-multiple showing canary rate vs expected weight, plus a drift alarm when observed_canary_rate deviates > 3x expected for 5m.
maria: agree. also UX change: in console when you create a canary, show "effective split" after normalization (i.e., after header/cookie priority applied) not just declared weight. users get confused otherwise.
kevin: minor edge: for A/B experiments we want stable stickiness across rollouts. so persist cohort_key -> experiment assignment in KV for 24h when cohort is ephemeral (no cookie). makes debugging easier.
anya: @kevin you mean tanya :)
tanya: yep. +1 on storing ephemeral assigns with TTL. need to watch capacity for high QPS endpoints though. maybe do sample-based persistence only for users showing high session counts.
maria: plan: 1) change canonical key impl and add residual bucket in staging; 2) add telemetry tags and new dashboard panels; 3) tweak console UX to show "effective split"; 4) run a small canary (1% residual) on staging for 48h.
kevin: create feature flag `route-stochastic-residual` and gate rollout. i'll open PR for murmur3 helper and config parsing.
maria: i'll add the dashboard and alerts. jon, can you coordinate a quick heatmap to show cohort_entropy across regions?
jon: on it. will push a query and a Grafana panel.
anya: deploy-bot: deploy staging config?
deploy-bot: staging deploy queued (build 8421). will notify on completion :rocket:
kevin: thanks — once staging looks good we float to canary and watch `routing.choice{was_residual=true}` and `observed_canary_rate`. if anything spikes revert the flag.
maria: sweet. adding an action item doc in the rollout board. :white_check_mark:
